MIN-CNSX-LIQ.*: Battery-metals demand (Co, Ni, Li) is driving expanded use of CYANEX-family extractants across new hydromet and recycling circuits. MIN-CUSX-LIQ.*: Copper SX reagent demand tracks global copper output from leach-SX-EW circuits, which are expanding as oxide ore grades decline and operators push secondary sulfide bioleaching. Syensqo and BASF dominate supply and pass through feedstock cost changes (phenol, kerosene) with multi-year supply agreements. Chinese-operated African copper mines are increasingly open to Kopper/Huaxing generics, but plant-level switching cost remains the strongest barrier — a reagent change requires circuit re-optimization and typically happens only during major plant refurbishments.

F27-VAN-PWD.*: Syensqo announced restart of its Saint-Fons (France) synthetic vanillin production unit in 2025, adding security of supply for European customers after a period of reliance on its US and China plants. Chinese vanillin export volumes remain strong but face periodic anti-dumping scrutiny in some markets. Guaiacol feedstock pricing has been stable but remains concentrated among few producers (BASF, Camlin). Bio-based vanillin (Borregaard lignin route, Syensqo Rhovanil Natural from ferulic acid) continues to grow as a premium segment driven by clean-label demand.

BCI-TEA-LIQ.*: TEA demand is driven by global cement production growth, particularly in emerging markets. Personal care demand is stable. Pricing tracks EO closely. Chinese ethanolamine capacity continues to expand but quality certification for cosmetic-grade TEA gives Western producers a margin advantage.

BCI-DEA-LIQ.*: DEA pricing tracks ethylene oxide. MDEA substitution in gas treating is gradually reducing DEA growth in the oil & gas segment. Cocamide DEA faces increasing scrutiny in personal care, with some major brands switching to MEA-based alternatives. Glyphosate DEA salt remains a stable demand anchor.

BCI-2EH-LIQ.*: 2-EH pricing closely tracks propylene. The shift from DEHP to DINP/DOTP plasticizers has modestly reduced 2-EH demand growth in the plasticizer segment, but acrylic ester (2-EHA) demand for adhesives and coatings continues to grow. Chinese 2-EH capacity expansion has pressured Asian spot markets.

BCI-ACRYL-LIQ.*: Acrylamide pricing tracks acrylonitrile (ACN) closely. SNF Group's dominant position gives it significant pricing power. Growing water treatment infrastructure investment in developing countries drives steady demand growth. Enhanced oil recovery (EOR) using PAM polymers is a swing demand factor tied to oil prices.

BCI-CACL2-LIQ.*: Calcium chloride demand is seasonal, with Q4-Q1 deicing demand driving pricing in North America and Europe. Oilfield demand has recovered with higher drilling activity. Chinese export volumes of flake CaCl₂ remain strong, competing with local production in Western markets on price.

BCI-NAPH-LIQ.*: Naphtha pricing tracks Brent crude closely. Asian naphtha demand remains strong from Korean, Japanese, and Chinese crackers. European naphtha demand is under structural pressure as crackers rationalize capacity. Middle East refiners increasingly export naphtha to Asia rather than upgrading to gasoline.

BCI-PRP-GAS.*: Chinese PDH overcapacity is depressing Asian propylene margins. US refinery FCC propylene output has declined as refiners shift to lighter crudes. European propylene remains tight due to cracker shutdowns and maintenance cycles.

BCI-ETH-GAS.*: US ethane advantage continues to drive cracker investment in the Gulf Coast. European naphtha crackers face structural cost pressure from both US ethane and Chinese coal-to-olefins capacity. Middle East ethane-fed capacity expansions (Saudi Arabia, UAE) add further supply.

BCI-BDO-LIQ.*: Chinese coal-to-BDO capacity expansion continues to pressure global pricing. BASF's integrated Reppe position in Ludwigshafen remains the Western benchmark. PTMEG/spandex demand from athletic wear and stretch fabrics is the key demand driver.

BCI-CL2-GAS.*: Chlorine pricing remains tied to the ECU balance — strong caustic soda demand from alumina refining and pulp mills has kept chlorine pricing under pressure in 2025-2026. European energy costs remain a key competitiveness factor for membrane-cell plants, with some producers idling capacity during peak electricity price periods. Chinese chlor-alkali capacity continues to expand, particularly in Xinjiang where cheap coal-fired electricity provides a structural cost advantage.
